doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Life on the Ellington bus
summary: Berry describes living with the band on the bus like a family with squabbles.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Share some of those with us. Share a couple of things.
Oh, I just can’t pull one out of the air you know. You’ve got to remind me about something. Just you know terribly funny things happen. Funny sayings — oh I can’t tell that one.
That’s something else. I’ll put it this way. If I do the same thing over again I would do it exactly the same.

But when you’re traveling with a big band, and say you’re on a bus, say Duke Ellington’s band. You’re on the bus with those 16 guys, whatever, you know perhaps 12 or more hours a day. Every day. For years, right? And you know you’re with them more than you’re with your own family. So there better be some humorous things going on, you know? It’s like you’re living with people that — it’s hard enough to live with your own family, let alone twenty other people’s families.

And some of these guys have been there with that band since before I was born. You know, long before I was born. And so like any family, they had their squabbles. You know you can’t live with people that intimately 24 hours a day is what it really amounts to, and half of it in a bus, I mean that enclosed quarters, where there’s no place to go, you know, you just have to pull the shade down beside you. MR: I know they have to play soon, but do you have anything maybe about Joe Williams that — was Joe Williams with the Ellington band when you were there?
